record.paper_title: Open Problems on Eigenvalues of the Laplacian
record.original_question: Let Ω be a bounded domain in ℝⁿ with Dirichlet Laplacian eigenvalues 0 < λ₁ < λ₂ ≤ ···. For every integer m ≥ 2, must λₘ₊₁/λₘ be at most the ball value j_{p+1,1}² / j_{p,1}², where p = (n−2)/2 and j_{ν,k} is the k-th positive zero of J_ν? In dimension 2, this asks whether λₘ₊₁/λₘ ≤ (λ₂/λ₁)_disk ≈ 2.5387 for all m ≥ 2.

evidence.quote: For Ω ⊂ ℝ² and all m ≥ 2 show that λₘ₊₁/λₘ ≤ (λ₂/λ₁)|disk ≈ 2.5387. In ℝⁿ this conjecture reads λₘ₊₁/λₘ ≤ j²_{p+1,1}/j²_{p,1}.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ ($n\ge 2$) be a bounded domain, and let $0<\lambda_1<\lambda_2\le\lambda_3\le\cdots$ denote the eigenvalues of the Dirichlet Laplacian on $\Omega$, i.e. the values $\lambda$ for which there exists a nonzero $u\in H^1_0(\Omega)$ with $-\Delta u=\lambda u$ in $\Omega$. For a real number $\nu>-1$, let $j_{\nu,k}$ denote the $k$-th positive zero of the Bessel function $J_\nu$. Set $p=(n-2)/2$.

Prove or disprove: for every bounded domain $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ and every integer $m\ge 2$,
$$\frac{\lambda_{m+1}(\Omega)}{\lambda_m(\Omega)}\;\le\;\frac{j_{p+1,1}^{\,2}}{j_{p,1}^{\,2}},$$
the value on the right-hand side being the ratio $\lambda_2/\lambda_1$ for a ball in $\mathbb{R}^n$. In particular, when $n=2$, decide whether
$$\frac{\lambda_{m+1}(\Omega)}{\lambda_m(\Omega)}\le\left(\frac{\lambda_2}{\lambda_1}\right)_{\text{disk}}\approx 2.5387\quad\text{for all }m\ge 2.$$
artifact.status_search_result: The case m=1 is the classical Payne–Pólya–Weinberger conjecture, proved by Ashbaugh and Benguria in the 1990s. The extension to consecutive ratios λ_{m+1}/λ_m for m≥2 remains an open conjecture; partial results and related strengthenings exist (e.g., work on lower-order Dirichlet eigenvalues and PPW-type results in symmetric spaces), but no full proof or counterexample for general bounded domains has appeared.

status_evidence.title: Proof of the Payne–Pólya–Weinberger conjecture (Ashbaugh–Benguria)
status_evidence.snippet: Ashbaugh and Benguria proved that the ball maximizes λ₂/λ₁ among bounded domains in ℝⁿ.

status_evidence.title: More Bounds on Eigenvalue Ratios for Dirichlet Laplacians in N Dimensions
status_evidence.snippet: Results which extend the proof of the PPW conjecture to ratios of higher eigenvalues.
status_evidence.claim: Only partial bounds are known for higher consecutive ratios; the sharp conjecture remains open.

status_evidence.title: On Ashbaugh–Benguria's Conjecture about Lower Order Dirichlet Eigenvalues of the Laplacian
status_evidence.snippet: Progress toward Ashbaugh–Benguria-type conjectures on lower-order eigenvalues.
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture for m≥2 is still being investigated as an open problem.
